messages:
jamie: Hey team - customer 'ZephyrApps' getting intermittent 429s on project zephyr even tho the project quota tile shows ~30% available. Invoice also reports ~65k tokens for the day, dashboard shows ~38k. Any ideas? :thinking:

adrian: Can you drop the org and project ids and a sample failing request? I'll pull enforcement logs.

jamie: org=o-42a9, project=p-zephyr. Sample curl that hits 429:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hi"}'
```

Response:
```json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": { "type": "rate_limit_error", "message": "quota exceeded", "meta": { "scope": "org_shared_pool", "window_ms": 600000, "window_remaining_ms": -23000 } } }
```

li: Thanks - that window_remaining_ms negative is telling. Dashboard project tile is showing remaining based on calendar-hour buckets for project-level view, but enforcement uses a rolling-window across the org shared pool. If another project in the same org burst, enforcement can take tokens from the shared pool and cause 429s for zephyr even if its project tile looks fine.

adrian: Confirmed in enforcement logs: at 1890011200 we had a burst from p-specter that consumed ~32k tokens in 4m. Enforcement applied org shared limit and then per-project rolling edits caused subsequent calls from p-zephyr to get 429 until the rolling window decayed.

maria: Is this a dashboard aggregation mismatch (calendar vs rolling) or an enforcement bug? Which one do we explain to the customer?

li: It's a mismatch between the visualization and enforcement semantics. Dash tiles are cheap to compute and show fixed buckets (calendar hour sliding), but runtime enforces a true rolling-window across the org's shared pool for fairness. Not a bug, but confusing UX.

adrian: Repro steps we used in staging to validate: 1) create two test projects under same org; 2) send a high-rate burst from project A (10k requests of 256 tokens over 3 min); 3) send steady low-rate requests from project B; 4) observe project B hits 429 while dashboard still shows quota for B. I can paste the load-generator command if helpful.

jamie: pls paste load-gen, will try to repro locally for customer.

adrian: Load-gen gist:
```bash
# burst from project A
seq 1 10000 | xargs -n1 -P200 curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_A" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"x"}'
# steady from project B
seq 1 1000 | xargs -n1 -P20 curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_B" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"y"}'
```

ops-bot: Observability note: at 1890011187 -> 1890011402 we saw a 5x spike on org o-42a9, top contributor p-specter (32.1k tokens). Cluster autoscale handled throughput but shared pool enforcement tripped.

jamie: I ran the reproduce with small scale, saw the same pattern: first ~80 requests fine, then ~429s for ~6 minutes until rolling window decayed.

maria: For customer message: explain that the project tile is not the enforcement source of truth for rolling quotas; recommend we (a) show org-level shared-pool consumption in dashboard, (b) expose rolling-window view, and (c) offer dedicated capacity or higher org pool for them.

adrian: Short-term mitigation for them: enable per-project reservation (dedicated capacity) or set higher org shared pool. Long term: product to add explicit "rolling-window" overlay on tiles. I'll create an internal ticket.

jamie: Thanks. I'll reply to the customer with the explanation, repro steps, and the mitigation options. Also asking for permission to provision temporary dedicated capacity while they evaluate. :thumbsup:
